claims.statement: Acceptance needs artifacts: a summary-only development proposal is rejected with `req_gate_no_evidence`, so approval requires a non-empty archived artifact plus a matching revision.

Integration is the development executor's job inside its own lane: it aligns with `origin/develop`, merges with `--no-ff`, re-verifies in the integration state, and only then pushes; the main session never integrates an iteration.
A requirement closes only when the artifact carries a `develop@<sha>`; a bare feature-branch push is not a closeout, and a SHA mismatch is rejected as `integration_bad_sha`.
Green on a feature branch does not transfer: the post-merge integration state must be verified again before `develop` is pushed.
An amend on a `done` requirement does not mutate history — it derives a new requirement whose receipt names the origin id, rev and closed reason.

Switching a capability on is a separate assertion from its existence: `*_ships_armed_*` cases pin that a config value is actually effective, because schema validates shape only and a required key may legally be `false` while the protection silently fails.
